stories.headline: Iran lets ships from India and China pass Hormuz freely
body: Iran has exempted ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar from its Strait of Hormuz restrictions, a senior lawmaker said.
He said the US does not stop those ships either.
Iran has largely shut the strait since the war began on 28 February.
stories.joke: A hall pass for the world's busiest oil lane.
stories.vc: Free passage for Indian ships lowers freight and insurance costs on India's oil imports.

stories.headline: Kenyan doomsday cult leader sentenced to 200 years
body: A Kenyan court sentenced pastor Paul Mackenzie to 200 years for the murders of 191 people.
He was convicted of ordering followers, mostly children, to starve themselves to death.
His cult is linked to over 400 deaths, and he faces more charges.
stories.vc: The case has pushed Kenya to look at stricter rules on how churches are registered and watched.

stories.headline: New wave of bomb threats hits flights across Europe
body: Officials across Europe reported a fresh wave of bomb threats against flights on Friday.
Three broadcasters also got threats; no bombs were found and no one was hurt.
It follows drone incursions and attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems.
stories.vc: Repeated hoaxes cost airlines money through diversions and raise security costs.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 1,718 points as Nifty reclaims 25,000
body: The Sensex rose 1,718 points (2.1%) and the Nifty closed above 25,000.
It was the seventh straight day of gains, Business Standard reported.
IT and bank shares led the rally.
stories.joke: Seven days up. The bulls are not taking leave this Diwali.
stories.vc: A seven-day rally lifts IPO and fundraising plans for Indian companies.

stories.headline: MakeMyTrip buys Bengaluru carpooling app Quick Ride
body: MakeMyTrip has bought a majority stake in Bengaluru-based carpooling startup Quick Ride.
The deal amount was not disclosed.
It takes the travel company into ride-pooling, alongside its bus and cab services.
stories.joke: Your flight, hotel and now your office carpool, one app.
stories.vc: Big travel platforms buying niche mobility startups gives founders a clear exit route.

stories.headline: TRAI backs phone service straight from satellites
body: TRAI recommended a new licence that lets satellites connect directly to mobile phones.
Telecom firms could use satellite partners to extend coverage, and satellite firms could sell capacity.
The licence would last up to 20 years with an 8% revenue fee.
stories.vc: Direct-to-phone satellite service opens a new market for Indian telcos and satellite startups.

stories.headline: Company AI spending stalls just as Anthropic nears IPO
body: Ramp data shows business spending on AI barely grew over late summer, up just 1.5% in August and September.
In July it had grown 42% in a month.
Firms use more AI, but price competition may be capping what they pay.
stories.joke: More AI, same bill. Finance teams are thrilled; AI labs less so.
stories.vc: If AI spending flattens, investors may rethink sky-high valuations for OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.headline: Fox completes its $22B purchase of Roku
body: Fox has completed its $22 billion deal to buy streaming company Roku.
Fox says the combined company is now the third-largest TV business in the US by viewership.
Roku's founder Anthony Wood says the teams will keep building as before.
stories.joke: Old TV buys new TV. Remote control included.
stories.vc: Traditional broadcasters buying streaming platforms shows where ad money is moving.

stories.headline: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027
body: Elon Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production next year.
The factory space will build more Cybercab robotaxis instead.
Musk once predicted 250,000 sales a year; Tesla sold only tens of thousands in total.
stories.joke: The truck that looked like the future is now history.
stories.vc: Tesla shifting factories to robotaxis shows its bet on autonomy over car sales.

stories.headline: Pentagon offers battery startup 6K a $250M loan
body: Battery-materials startup 6K won conditional approval for a $250 million Defense Department loan.
It will build a Tennessee factory using a microwave-powered process.
The aim is battery materials that don't depend on Chinese suppliers.
stories.vc: Defence money is becoming a major funding source for battery and climate-tech startups.

stories.headline: Physicl raises $10M to train robots in realistic simulations
body: Physicl raised a $10 million seed round led by Inovia Capital.
It builds realistic digital worlds to help train robots and AI world models.
Its founder turned his old 3D product-imaging team to this new use.
stories.joke: Robots get a video game to practise in.
stories.vc: Simulation tools are a fast-growing bet as investors pour money into robotics.

stories.statLabel: woman president of the Navajo Nation
stories.headline: Navajo Nation elects its first woman president
body: Crystalyne Curley is set to become the first woman president of the Navajo Nation.
She was also its first woman council speaker and has worked on water rights and uranium clean-up.
The Seneca Nation also elected its first woman president, Tina Abrams.
stories.vc: Tribal leaders control key decisions on land, water and energy projects.

stories.statLabel: days to transfer after police complaint
stories.headline: Tiruvannamalai professor moved after nursing student alleges harassment
body: A 20-year-old nursing student accused a senior professor at Tiruvannamalai Medical College of sexual harassment.
He was transferred two days after she went to the police.
She says the college's internal complaints committee failed to inquire properly.
stories.vc: Weak complaint committees put institutions at legal risk under India's workplace harassment law.

stories.headline: Abuse survivors became a political force in the midterms
body: Advocates call the midterms a win for survivors of sexual violence.
In Ohio, an ad attacking Amy Acton over her childhood abuse backfired, and she won by 8 points.
Some candidates accused of abuse also withdrew.
stories.vc: Campaigns that misjudge survivor voters risk wasting millions on ads, as Ohio showed.

stories.headline: AIIMS Awantipora to open its OPD before December
body: AIIMS Awantipora in Kashmir aims to start outpatient services before December, Health Minister JP Nadda said.
Inpatient services are planned for July 2027, with MBBS classes from 2027-28.
Equipment worth ₹59.41 crore has been approved.
stories.vc: A full AIIMS in the Valley cuts long trips to Delhi or Chandigarh for specialist care.

stories.headline: IHH wants over half of Fortis, bringing ₹10,000 crore
body: Malaysia's IHH Healthcare wants to raise its Fortis stake from 31% to over 50%, Fortis said.
That could bring about ₹10,000 crore of new capital into Fortis over time.
Fortis says a court-ordered forensic audit does not block the move.
stories.vc: More capital from IHH could fund faster bed expansion for one of India's biggest chains.

stories.headline: Bengaluru cancer chain HCG adds 146 beds this year
body: HCG added 25 beds last quarter, in Kenya, Kolkata and Nagpur, and 146 in the first half of the year.
Revenue rose 16% to ₹732 crore.
Robotic surgeries were up 37%.
stories.vc: Specialist cancer chains are expanding as more Indians get diagnosed and treated.

stories.headline: Paras Health's new Srinagar and Kanpur hospitals double revenue
body: Paras Healthcare's new hospitals in Srinagar and Kanpur more than doubled their revenue to ₹84.4 crore.
Company profit rose 3.3 times to ₹40.4 crore.
Bed occupancy climbed to 73% from 59%.
stories.vc: Fast-filling hospitals in smaller cities support more expansion in under-served markets.

stories.headline: New champion Antonelli tops Friday practice in Brazil
body: Kimi Antonelli was fastest in second practice at Interlagos, ahead of Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.
His best lap was 1m10.763s on soft tyres.
Teammate George Russell takes a five-place grid penalty for a new engine.
stories.joke: Champion on Sunday, still fastest on Friday.
stories.vc: Mercedes needs just three more points than Ferrari here to lock in the constructors' title and its prize money.
